Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) Held in Mumbai on 23 November 2026
articles.full_content:
The The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as the Knowledge Partner, organised a “Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP)” on 23 November 2026 at Mumbai. Following the release of revised series of GDP, CPI and IIP at different points during 2026, the conference was organised to familiarise data users with the methodological changes, data sources and key improvements incorporated in each of the revised series. It also aimed to facilitate a better understanding of these changes and their implications for the resulting estimates.
The conference brought together representatives of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), SEBI, economists, forecasters, credit rating agencies, experts from financial institutions and the banking sector, academia, research institutions, industry and investor organisations, users of official statistics and senior officials of the Central and State Governments. The inaugural session comprised welcome remarks by Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI; the setting of the context by Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; the inaugural address by Dr. Poonam Gupta, Deputy Governor, RBI; the keynote address by Shri Deepak Parekh, Former Chairman, HDFC; and the vote of thanks by Shri Siddhartha Kundu, ADG, National Accounts Division, MoSPI. A booklet containing brief concept notes on the revised series of these indices was shared with the participants.
Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), in his welcome address, noted that macroeconomic statistics form the foundation of economic analysis, policy making and informed decision making and that GDP, CPI and IIP together provide a comprehensive measure of economic activity and growth. He observed that, as the structure of the economy, production processes, consumption patterns and technology continue to evolve, the statistical system must evolve continuously to remain representative of prevailing economic realities. He recalled that MoSPI had completed the base revision of these three indicators and launched the new series during 2026, with greater use of administrative and survey-based data, wider coverage and important methodological improvements and acknowledged the contribution of expert committees, central ministries, State Governments, RBI and other institutions.
Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, while setting the context, noted that the conference was being held in Mumbai after about a year, this time after the completion of the base revision exercise, with the first-quarter GDP estimates of the new series already released and the second-quarter estimates due shortly. He stated that the two-year exercise had been made possible by the support of several expert committees, other ministries and departments, State Governments, the RBI and other regulatory agencies. Air Fest 2026 showcases Indian Air Force's skill, valour and aerial excellence in Nagpur
articles.full_content:
Union Minister Nitin Gadkari graces Air Fest 2026 on Sunday; event showcases Indian Air Force’s aerial prowess and operational capabilities
By PIB Mumbai, Nagpur.
22 November 2026
Headquarters Maintenance Command, Indian Air Force, organised a spectacular air show at Vayusena Nagar, Nagpur, as part of the three-day Air Fest 2026. The event witnessed the participation of more than 16,000 spectators and showcased the operational capabilities, professionalism and traditions of the Indian Air Force through aerial displays, Special Forces demonstrations, precision drills and musical performances.
On colcluding day (Sunday, 22 November 2026), Shri Nitin Gadkari, Hon’ble Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, participated in the event as the Chief Guest. He was received by Air Marshal Yalla Umesh, VSM, PhD, Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Maintenance Command.
The Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team enthralled spectators with its aerial manoeuvres and synchronised formations. The Sarang Helicopter Display Team, flying indigenous Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopters, demonstrated the agility and manoeuvrability of the aircraft through spectacular aerial formations. The Akash Ganga skydiving team captivated the audience with free-fall and parachute displays. A major attraction was the flypast by three Su-30 fighter aircraft in victory formation, along with an impressive Paramotor Display.
The Garud Special Forces team conducted a slithering demonstration, showcasing its specialised skills and operational preparedness. The Air Warrior Drill Team presented an impressive display of synchronised drill and discipline. The No. 5 Air Force Band added to the celebrations with martial tunes and patriotic melodies. The event also featured a static display of Indian Air Force aviation assets, giving visitors an opportunity to see various IAF platforms and learn about their capabilities.
The three-day Air Fest received an overwhelming response, with more than 16,000 spectators attending the event. A large number of visitors, particularly NCC cadets, school and college students, participated enthusiastically. The event provided an opportunity for young people to witness the professionalism, dedication and capabilities of the Indian Air Force. The displays also highlighted the importance of teamwork, discipline, technological advancement and indigenous capabilities in strengthening the nation's air power.
Air Fest 2026 also served as a public outreach initiative to strengthen the bond between the Indian Air Force and citizens. It aimed to inspire the younger generation to consider a career in the Indian Air Force, foster patriotism and create awareness about the role and contributions of the IAF in safeguarding the nation.
The successful conduct of Air Fest 2026 reaffirmed Headquarters Maintenance Command's commitment to public outreach and youth engagement, while providing citizens an opportunity to witness the capabilities and traditions of the Indian Air Force.
Saurabh

The event witnessed the participation of more than 16,000 spectators and showcased the operational capabilities, professionalism and traditions of the Indian Air Force through aerial displays, Special Forces demonstrations, precision drills and musical performances.

MSME-DFO Gangtok Facilitates Participation of 10 PM Vishwakarma Artisans in GO SADAM 2.0 Festival at Sadam Hills
articles.full_content:
Gangtok, 21 November 2026
The MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Gangtok, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, today participated in the three-day local festival “GO SADAM 2.0”, being held from 21st to 23rd November, 2026, at Sikkim Natural Theme Park, Sadam Hills, South Sikkim, to promote local entrepreneurship and provide market exposure to traditional artisans.
As part of the initiative, MSME-DFO, Gangtok facilitated the participation of 10 PM Vishwakarma artisans, who showcased and sold their traditional handmade products through dedicated stalls at the festival. The initiative provided an important platform for the artisans to directly interact with visitors, tourists and potential customers and explore new marketing opportunities.
GO SADAM 2.0 was organised by Sadam Sukrabarey & Gupti Tourism Development Society in association with Himalayan Footprints Tourism Cooperative Society as a three-day tourism, cultural and recreational festival. The festival featured paragliding, stargazing, science-related activities, fitness competitions, local exhibitions and live musical performances across Public Ground Sukrabarey, Gupti School Ground and Rameytay Dara take-off point.
The festival was formally inaugurated by the local area MLA, Shri N.B. Pradhan, and the Hon’ble MLA of Namchi-Singhitham Constituency, Shri Satish Rai, along with the Zilla Adhyaksha and other distinguished dignitaries.
During their visit to the exhibition area, the dignitaries visited the stalls set up by the PM Vishwakarma artisans, interacted with them, appreciated their traditional craftsmanship and took keen interest in the products displayed.
The participation provided direct market access, product promotion, customer interaction, business networking and entrepreneurial encouragement to the artisans. It also helped in integrating traditional artisanship with tourism and local economic development activities in Sikkim.
The participation of PM Vishwakarma artisans in GO SADAM 2.0 reflects the continued efforts of MSME-DFO, Gangtok towards promotion of micro-enterprises, traditional artisans and local products, and towards enhancing market access, encouraging self-employment and strengthening the economic empowerment of artisans in Sikkim.
